facts: At 10:04 UTC, the checkout error-rate alert fired.
Deployment dep-1842 for checkout-api completed at 10:01 UTC.
Database latency increased at approximately the same time as the error spike.
The external payment provider reported intermittent errors.
A previous incident with similar symptoms involved an expired service credential.
The incident director has asked for a likely cause and a rollback recommendation.
The brief is based on initial reports, not a confirmed timeline or root cause.
assumptions: The 3-minute gap between deployment completion (10:01 UTC) and alert firing (10:04 UTC) suggests possible but unconfirmed correlation.
Database latency increase and error spike are assumed to be related in time, but causal direction is unknown.
The external payment provider's reported errors are assumed to potentially overlap with the observed checkout failures, though the overlap percentage is unknown.
It is assumed the current incident could be a recurrence of the prior credential-expiration issue, but this has not been verified.
It is assumed no other checkout-api changes or infrastructure events occurred in this window besides dep-1842.

hypotheses.claim: Deployment dep-1842 introduced a defect that caused the checkout error-rate spike.
supporting_evidence: Deployment completed at 10:01 UTC, only 3 minutes before the alert fired at 10:04 UTC.
Checkout-api is the directly deployed service exhibiting the failures.
contradicting_evidence: No log or error-trace evidence yet confirms the failures originate from application code changed in dep-1842.
Concurrent database latency and payment provider issues offer alternative explanations.

hypotheses.claim: Increased database latency caused or contributed to the checkout failures.
supporting_evidence: Database latency increased at approximately the same time as the error spike.
contradicting_evidence: No data yet establishes whether latency increase preceded, followed, or was caused by the error spike (e.g., could be a downstream symptom of the deployment).
Exact timing correlation has not been confirmed.

hypotheses.claim: The external payment provider's intermittent errors are driving some or all of the checkout failures.
supporting_evidence: The payment provider independently reported intermittent errors around the incident window.
contradicting_evidence: No breakdown yet shows what fraction of the 9% failure rate is payment-related versus other checkout steps.
Provider issues may be coincidental and unrelated to internal checkout failures.

hypotheses.claim: An expired service credential (similar to a prior incident) is causing authentication or authorization failures.
supporting_evidence: A previous incident with similar symptoms was traced to an expired service credential.
contradicting_evidence: No confirmation yet that any credential has expired in this incident.
Pattern similarity to a past incident is not direct evidence of the same cause recurring.

missing_information: Checkout-api error logs and stack traces from the incident window.
Whether the database latency spike preceded or followed the checkout error spike (precise timestamps).
Percentage of the 9% failure rate attributable to payment provider errors versus internal errors.
Current status of relevant service credentials (expired or valid).
Whether other services or dependencies were affected simultaneously.
Historical baseline for database latency to determine if the increase is anomalous.
Rollback risk assessment for dep-1842 (e.g., data migrations, breaking changes).
reversible_next_actions: Pull and review checkout-api application logs and error traces for the incident window to identify failure signatures.
Check the expiration status of relevant service credentials used by checkout-api.
Correlate precise timestamps of database latency increase against the error-rate spike to determine sequence.
Contact the payment provider for detailed incident timing and affected transaction volume.
Review the diff/changelog for dep-1842 to identify potential breaking changes.
Prepare a rollback of dep-1842 as a ready contingency without executing it until more evidence is gathered.
Set up a short monitoring window (e.g., 5-10 minutes) to observe whether error rate trends change independent of any action, to help isolate cause.

uncertainty.reason: Multiple plausible contributing factors (deployment, database latency, payment provider, credential) occurred in close temporal proximity, but the brief explicitly states this is based on initial reports without a confirmed timeline or root cause, and no log-level or causal evidence yet isolates a single source.
